lessons: Multiword phrases whose target is a genuine prerequisite should be linked even in examples, while isolated generic nouns such as set, measure, and distribution remain false positives.
Distribution is ambiguous across probability and functional analysis; a probability distribution can link to distribution-law only when the surrounding probability context establishes that meaning.
A specialized recurring phrase such as normal distribution or uniform distribution is a definition-gap signal, not permission to link to a broad distribution-law target.
A target already linked in the core may be omitted on later repetitions unless the later occurrence introduces a distinct construction where expansion is useful.

The link audit does not by itself justify rewriting prerequisite metadata: theorem consequences and contextual comparisons should remain ordinary links unless the target is required to parse the definition.
